findings.desc: overflow_auto bypasses its documented visible-approval guard: core/lattice-dispatch starts the dispatch when either approve=true or start=true is present, so --start=true alone materializes dispatch state even though the CLI/docs promise suggest-only behavior unless visibly approved. This breaks the manual-first user-visible contract for overflow_auto.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 74ce419c. overflow_auto now requires approve=true and start=true; fake dispatch paths are bounded before any file write; scaffolded real-host dispatch creates the projected worktree or returns failed with warnings. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, npm --prefix packages/main run test:dispatch-run-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:lattice-handoff-smoke, npm run test:command-ownership-contract, and npm run test:process-fact-contract.

findings.desc: [HIGH] packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:845 and 1054-1066 leave approved real-host dispatch_run/overflow_auto without a usable overflow worktree. prepareDispatch writes only metadata and explicitly leaves worktree creation undone, but the scaffolded real-host run path tells the operator to run codex/claude/gemini in .worktrees/overflow/... anyway. Repro: node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root <tmp> lattice dispatch run --storyId=B-real --host=codex --json returned status=needs_receipt with nextAction pointing at .worktrees/overflow/B-real/D-B-real-codex-..., while the recorded dispatch.json showed worktreeExists=false for that path. That breaks the required host-overflow workflow in docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md:52-54, where Lattice must project an isolated overflow worktree before the host works in it, so the approved real-host overflow path cannot actually execute.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: overflow_auto starts a mutating dispatch when either --start=true or --approve=true is present because the guard is `if (args.start !== true && args.approve !== true) return plan`. That contradicts the CLI contract (`requires visible approval to start`) and CHK-008 requireApproval semantics. Repro: a throwaway registry run returned lattice.dispatch_run.v1 accepted_local for both startOnly={start:true} and approveOnly={approve:true}. The command currently bypasses its explicit approval/start safety policy.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: fake dispatch_run writes pack.allowedPaths[0] directly via path.join(worktreeAbs, markerPath) before any scope validation, so ../../ traversal escapes the isolated overflow worktree. Repro: a throwaway registry run with allowedPaths=["../../escape.txt"] created .worktrees/overflow/escape.txt and only failed later at git add. This breaks the bounded-path contract for dispatch_run/overflow_auto and allows out-of-scope filesystem writes.

findings.desc: Verified HIGH: 74ce419c still allows fake dispatch_run to write outside the isolated overflow worktree via tracked symlink paths. The new assertWorktreeRelativePath()/normalizeFakePackPaths guard in packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts only rejects absolute and .. segments, but runFakeLeafDispatch then resolves markerAbs and writes it directly before any canonical-path check. Repro: after npm --prefix packages/main run build, a one-off registry run in a temporary git repo with a tracked absolute symlink packages/main/src/generated/escape-link -> /tmp/... prepared dispatchId=D-symlink with allowedPaths=["packages/main/src/generated/escape-link/escaped.txt"]. dispatch_run threw later at git add with fatal: pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link, but /tmp/.../escaped.txt had already been created with dispatch metadata. This means the bounded fake-path write contract is still bypassable before the command fails.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 990be1be. Fake dispatch now uses canonical realpath containment before mkdir/write so symlink escapes fail before external writes. README and host-overflow docs now describe landed dispatch_plan/prepare/run/overflow_auto, approve+start gating, and real-host worktree creation/failure behavior. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, command ownership contract, and process fact contract.

findings.desc: README.md:76, README.md:99, docs/requirements/decisions/host-overflow.md:35 MEDIUM: docs still present dispatch_plan/dispatch_prepare/dispatch_run as future work and only show the older handoff/host_dispatch flow, but the local CLI/code already ship overflow_auto with a visible approve+start gate and dispatch_run that creates a real-host worktree before needs_receipt or returns failed on scaffold errors. Update the docs to describe the landed dispatch surfaces and these approval/worktree semantics.

findings.desc: Real-host dispatch_run can scaffold an isolated overflow worktree while preserving allowedPaths/deniedPaths that point outside that worktree, so the generated prompt can instruct a real host to edit ../outside.txt. Fake dispatch paths are bounded, but real-host scaffold does not validate pack paths before writing prompt/worktree metadata or returning needs_receipt. Repro: prepare a codex dispatch with allowedPaths=["../outside.txt"], run dispatch_run, then inspect .koala/dispatches/<dispatchId>/prompt.md; it contains "Only edit these paths: ../outside.txt" while the worktree is .worktrees/overflow/<story>/<dispatch>.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit b7b16fcf. Dispatch pack allowedPaths/deniedPaths are now normalized before prompt metadata is persisted, and real-host scaffold revalidates paths against the actual worktree before returning needs_receipt. Smoke now covers real-host traversal rejection before metadata persists and real-host symlink escape rejection before needs_receipt. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, host-overflow smoke, command ownership contract, process fact contract, git diff --check, and lattice validate test command output.

findings.desc: dispatchId path traversal escapes .koala/dispatches and allows out-of-scope Lattice metadata writes. dispatchDir/dispatchFile join caller-controlled dispatchId into storage paths, and prepareDispatch accepts args.dispatchId from the public handler unchanged. Repro: dispatch_prepare --dispatchId=../../../outside/owned writes dispatch.json, pack.json, prompt.md, and transcript.log outside the repository dispatch storage root. Apply validation to all public dispatchId read/write paths and add smoke coverage for malicious dispatchId.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit b7b16fcf. dispatchId is now validated at the storage helper/read-write boundary and rejected for empty, absolute, separator, or traversal values across prepare/run/status/collect/receipt/resume/cancel/review/merge_plan. Smoke now covers malicious dispatchId rejection across those commands and proves no metadata is written outside .koala/dispatches. Verified with build, dispatch-run smoke, lattice-handoff smoke, host-overflow smoke, command ownership contract, process fact contract, git diff --check, and lattice validate test command output.
